from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars just show simple magnitude.",
            "Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.",
            "A cat's speed is a scalar.",
            "Velocity towards a bowl is a vector.",
            "Think of vectors as directional arrows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Fundamentals of Vectors: Directions and Magnitudes", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(dot))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00FFFF")
        arrow.move_to(dot.get_center())
        self.play(Transform(dot, arrow))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label = Text("Vector has magnitude and direction", font_size=20, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Indicate(arrow))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(dot), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(arrow))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition (The Parallelogram Rule)", [
            "Connect vectors tail-to-head for addition.",
            "The resultant vector completes the parallelogram.",
            "It shows the actual path taken."
        ])
        
        # Colors for vectors
        vec_a_col = "#FF6B6B"
        vec_b_col = "#4ECDC4"
        vec_c_col = "#FFE66D"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(vec_a_col)
        
        vec_a = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=vec_a_col, buff=0)
        vec_b = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.2 + RIGHT*0.5, color=vec_b_col, buff=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(vec_a, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(vec_b, 'D2')
        
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(vec_b_col)
        
        # Shift B to head of A
        vec_b_shifted = vec_b.copy()
        vec_b_shifted.move_to(vec_a.get_end() + (vec_b.get_end() - vec_b.get_start())/2)
        
        # Draw resultant C
        vec_c = Arrow(start=vec_a.get_start(), end=vec_b_shifted.get_end(), color=vec_c_col, buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            vec_b.animate.shift(vec_a.get_end() - vec_b.get_start()),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(Create(vec_c))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(vec_c_col)
        
        # Highlight C
        self.play(Indicate(vec_c))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Scalars change vector magnitude.", "Positive scalars keep the same direction.", "Negative scalars reverse the direction."]
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication and Scaling", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Mobjects
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#90EE90")
        vector_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#90EE90").next_to(vector, UP)
        
        # Initial state
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(vector, vector_label), "C3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vector), Write(vector_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#90EE90"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        c = MathTex("c = 2", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(c, "B1")
        
        vector_scaled = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*4, color="#FFFF00")
        vector_scaled_label = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}", color="#FFFF00").next_to(vector_scaled, UP)
        
        self.play(Write(c))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Transform(vector, vector_scaled), Transform(vector_label, vector_scaled_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        c_neg = MathTex(r"c = -1", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(c_neg, "B1")
        
        vector_neg = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*2, color="#FF0000")

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(Transform(vector, vector_neg), Transform(vector_label, vector_neg_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors underpin physics and gaming.", "They define motion and positions.", "These basics build complex systems."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        summary = Text("Vectors: The Language of Motion", font_size=32, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(summary, "B3")
        self.play(Write(summary))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        
        car = Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        velocity_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#00CED1")
        car_group = VGroup(car, velocity_arrow)
        self.place_at_grid(car_group, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(car_group))
        self.play(car_group.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        complex_systems = Text("Physics, Games, AI", font_size=36, color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(complex_systems, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(complex_systems))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(summary), FadeOut(car_group), FadeOut(complex_systems))

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: Directions and Magnitudes
outline.target_audience: High school students or beginners in STEM

sections.title: The Concept of Vectors vs. Scalars
sections.content: Introduce scalars as simple magnitudes (e.g., speed) versus vectors, which carry both magnitude and direction (e.g., velocity). Use a coordinate system to define a vector as an arrow from an origin.
sections.example: A cat running: 'Speed' is 5m/s (scalar), but 'Velocity' is 5m/s towards the food bowl (vector).

sections.title: Visualizing Vector Components
sections.content: Break down a 2D vector into its x (horizontal) and y (vertical) components using the Cartesian plane. Explain how any vector can be expressed as a combination of basis vectors i and j.
sections.example: A drone flying diagonally. If it moves 3 units right and 4 units up, we represent this as the vector [3, 4].

sections.title: Vector Addition (The Parallelogram Rule)
sections.content: Explain how to add two vectors visually by placing the tail of one vector at the head of the other. Show the resultant vector forming the diagonal of a parallelogram.
sections.example: A boat crossing a river: One vector is the boat's engine power, the other is the river's current. The resultant vector shows the actual path taken.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication and Scaling
sections.content: Describe how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without altering its direction (unless the scalar is negative, which reverses it).
sections.example: A laser pointer: Multiplying a vector by 2 doubles the length of the light beam, keeping it pointing at the same target on the wall.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts. Conclude by highlighting how these basics are the foundation for game development, physics engines, and AI machine learning.
sections.example: Character movement in a video game: Calculating the final position of a character by adding 'velocity' vectors over time.
